from_quote: the various other reasons which I offered you in my last number
rationale: The paragraph refers to Cato's "last number", Cato 3, and its reasons drawn from "the vast extent of America".

from_quote: The executive power as described in the 2d article, consists of a president and vice-president, who are to hold their offices during the term of four years
rationale: The paragraph names "the 2d article" and describes its opening clause: a president and vice-president holding office "during the term of four years".
to_quote: He shall hold his Office during the Term of four Years

from_quote: established the qualifications of the president
rationale: In its summary of "the 2d article", the paragraph names the clause that sets the qualifications of the president.

from_quote: it also provides against the removal, death, or inability of the president and vice-president
rationale: In its summary of "the 2d article", the paragraph names the clause providing for the removal, death or inability of the president and vice-president.
to_quote: Removal, Death, Resignation or Inability, both of the President and Vice President

from_quote: regulates the salary of the president
rationale: In its summary of "the 2d article", the paragraph names the clause on the president's compensation ("the salary of the president").

from_quote: declares the causes for which the president and vice-president shall be removed from office
rationale: In its summary of "the 2d article", the paragraph names its last provision, the causes for which the president and vice-president "shall be removed from office".

from_quote: the first paragraph of the first section of the second article
rationale: The paragraph identifies the clause by number as "the first paragraph of the first section of the second article" and discusses the election of a president and vice-president for terms of four years.

from_quote: the unrestrained power of granting pardons for treason
rationale: The paragraph names the president's power of "granting pardons", which is in the first clause of Article II, Section 2.
to_quote: Power to grant Reprieves and Pardons

from_quote: his power of nomination and influence on all appointments
rationale: The paragraph names the president's "power of nomination" to appointments, which is in the second clause of Article II, Section 2.

from_quote: The ten miles square, which is to become the seat of government
rationale: The paragraph names "the ten miles square, which is to become the seat of government", the district described in Article I, Section 8, clause 17.

from_quote: This officer, for want of other employment, is made president of the senate
rationale: The paragraph names the provision that the vice-president "is made president of the senate".
to_quote: The Vice President of the United States shall be President of the Senate

from_quote: it is only necessary that he should be taken from the highest of five
rationale: The paragraph names the rule of the electoral clause by which the president may be chosen from "the highest of five".
to_quote: from the five highest on the List

from_quote: he has the power of receiving ambassadors
rationale: The paragraph names the president's power of "receiving ambassadors", which is in Article II, Section 3.

from_quote: as also to make treaties, leagues, and alliances with foreign states, assisted by the Senate
rationale: The paragraph names the president's power to make treaties "assisted by the Senate", which is in the second clause of Article II, Section 2.

from_quote: which when made become the supreme law of land
rationale: The paragraph names the provision that treaties, once made, "become the supreme law of land" (sic).
to_quote: shall be the supreme Law of the Land

from_quote: every bill which shall pass the House of Representatives and Senate is to be presented to him for approbation ; if he approves of it he is to sign it, if he disapproves he is to return it with objections
rationale: The paragraph describes in close wording the clause by which every bill passed by both houses is presented to the president, who signs it or returns it with objections.
to_quote: Every Bill which shall have passed the House of Representatives and the Senate

from_quote: he may pardon all offences, except in cases of impeachment
rationale: The paragraph names the pardon power with its exception "except in cases of impeachment", from the first clause of Article II, Section 2.
